name: @baton/core
//: Exports point at dist, not src, because apps/worker and apps/web run as `node dist/main.js` in their containers. Consequence: core must be built before the apps run, which tsc project references handle for typecheck and the Dockerfiles handle for runtime.
//exports.db/testing: The integration test harness. A separate entry point, deliberately not re-exported from ./db, so test-only code that truncates every table cannot load in a production container. Note: comment keys must stay OUT of `exports` — Node rejects an exports object mixing '.'-prefixed subpaths with plain keys.
//exports.env: The dotenv loader for CLI and dev entry points. A subpath rather than a barrel export because it reads the filesystem: the barrel is imported by `use client` components in apps/web, and a `node:fs` import reachable from a client bundle survives only on tree-shaking. Long-running services must not call it at all — a container silently absorbing a stray .env is how you deploy against the wrong database.
//exports.constants+redact: The two entry points a browser bundle may import. The barrel re-exports `normalise.js`, which imports `node:crypto`, so a `use client` component importing the barrel fails the webpack build outright — not tree-shaken away, because webpack resolves the scheme before it shakes anything. `constants.ts` and `redact.ts` have zero imports of their own, so these subpaths are safe by construction rather than by luck, and that is the property to preserve: if either ever grows a Node import, apps/web stops building and the rule has enforced itself.
